outcome: Decrease in hemoglobin values at 6 hours postoperatively
cohort: 66 patients diagnosed with endogenous type Cesarean Scar Pregnancy (CSP) who received ultrasound-assisted suction curettage treatment in an early pregnancy service between January 2012 and March 2019.
finding: Modified suction curettage (Group 2) resulted in a significantly smaller decrease in postoperative hemoglobin and a lower treatment failure rate compared to classical suction curettage (Group 1) for Cesarean Scar Pregnancy (CSP).
followup_time: Short-term postoperative follow-up, with specific mention of 6 hours postoperatively for hemoglobin measurement.
